items.headline: Over 782,000 seniors to get up to S$1,500 CPF top-up by Dec 8
items.summary: More than 782,000 citizens aged 50 and above will get a CPF top-up of up to S$1,500 by Dec 8, costing about S$1.04 billion; credited automatically, no application needed.

items.headline: Woman, 33, arrested over repeated rubbish-chute fires at a Punggol block
items.summary: A 33-year-old woman was arrested on Nov 18 after repeated rubbish-chute fires at Block 657B Punggol East; she faces a mischief-by-fire charge carrying up to seven years' jail.

items.headline: Singaporean couple charged with lying about their address to enrol their daughter in a top school
items.summary: A Singaporean couple aged 33 and 39 were charged on Nov 19 with giving false address information to enrol their daughter in a popular primary school; they return to court on Jan 7, 2027.

items.headline: Pakistan minister visits India for the first time since the 2025 war for an SCO forum
items.summary: Pakistan's climate minister Musadik Malik attended the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, inaugurated by PM Modi on Nov 20; the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the May 2025 war.

items.headline: Foreign investors pour a record US$9.6 billion into Indian stocks in November
items.summary: Global funds bought a net US$9.6 billion of Indian equities in November, a record monthly sum beating November 2020, as investors rotate out of AI-heavy markets; India reclaimed a top-five global market spot.

items.headline: India's October inflation hits a two-year high, raising the odds of a December rate rise
items.summary: India's retail inflation hit about a two-year high in October, breaching the top of the Reserve Bank's 2%-6% band; economists see a December rate rise as increasingly likely, a risk to the Nifty rally.

items.headline: Burnham seals an EU-UK 'reset' deal a decade after Brexit, claiming a 0.5% GDP boost
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham's office said a UK-EU 'reset' deal was sealed at a Brussels summit on Nov 20, with a youth mobility scheme for up to 100,000 under-30s each side and eased trade checks; Farage called him 'naive'.

items.headline: Health leaders warn Burnham's youth-jobs reforms could worsen NHS staffing
items.summary: NHS trust leaders warned that PM Burnham's drive to move more young people into work could leave the health service short of senior staff as trusts face higher apprenticeship costs. Reported by Bloomberg.

items.headline: Update: Russia hits Ukraine with 110-plus missiles hours after the APEC summit, violating Polish airspace
items.summary: Hours after the Trump-Xi-Putin summit, Russia struck Ukraine with more than 110 missiles, killing at least eight and damaging three Kyiv bridges; Poland scrambled NATO jets after an airspace violation and Putin said there would be 'no negotiations'.

items.headline: Estonia to shut its road borders with Russia for six months over a GRU-linked arson plot
items.summary: Estonia approved a preliminary six-month closure of all road crossings with Russia from Dec 1 after a foiled GRU-linked arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems; eight were detained and Moscow decried a 'new Iron Curtain'.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port as Houthis threaten Jeddah and Riyadh
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition struck Yemen's Hodeidah port in what an Al Jazeera correspondent called the heaviest raids of the war; the Houthis threatened Jeddah, Red Sea ports, and Riyadh's financial district.

items.headline: Cost-of-living protests spread across at least eight European countries
items.summary: Protests over living costs, military spending, and climate hit at least eight European countries on Nov 20, inspired by France's wave where unions seek a 10% minimum-wage rise; turnouts in the tens and hundreds of thousands.

items.headline: US regulators are reportedly investigating Nvidia's accounting
items.summary: SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia, Reuters reported, tied to a 2025 change dropping Singapore from its revenue breakdown; shares fell about 14% on Nov 20. Reported by Bloomberg and CNBC.

items.headline: US approved nearly 880,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China, House records show
items.summary: US Commerce records released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee show approval of 879,868 Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips for China across 21 licences, out of 3.4 million requested; Tencent cleared for 150,000. Reported by Bloomberg.

items.headline: Google gives its Gemini app the ability to control a Mac for you
items.summary: Google added computer-use to its Gemini app on Nov 19, letting the assistant take agentic control of a Mac to carry out tasks, alongside a wider rollout of Gemini 'Tasks'. Reported by TechCrunch.

items.headline: Nvidia details when it will, and won't, keep financing AI 'neocloud' buildouts
items.summary: Nvidia detailed when it will and will not backstop AI 'neocloud' buildouts, putting its guarantee for OpenAI's Pike County, Ohio campus at up to US$105 billion, down from an earlier figure near US$250 billion. Reported by TechCrunch.

items.headline: Wall Street's selloff deepens as the Nasdaq turns negative for 2026
items.summary: US stocks fell again on Nov 20: CNBC reported the S&P 500 down about 3.7% to around 6,910 (a seventh straight decline) and the Nasdaq down about 5.3% to around 22,618, turning negative for the year; the Dow fell roughly 950 points.

items.headline: Intuit cuts its FY27 outlook and sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
items.summary: Intuit beat Q1 estimates but cut its FY27 revenue-growth outlook to 8-9%, sending shares down about 7%; the same day it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about US$3.68 billion, under a third of the ~US$12 billion it paid in 2021.

items.headline: AI credit stress spreads as default-swap costs on Oracle and CoreWeave jump
items.summary: The tech selloff spread into credit on Nov 20, with Bloomberg reporting Oracle's five-year CDS at about 328 bps and CoreWeave's jumping to about 1,233 bps, implying default odds above 65% over five years.

items.headline: Treasury yields fall sharply as investors flee stocks for safe havens
items.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield fell more than 11 bps to about 4.94% on Nov 20 as investors fled stocks for bonds, even as fears of a December rate move weighed on risk assets. Reported by CNBC.

items.headline: Russell tops a wet Las Vegas practice as F1 heads into Sunday's race
items.summary: George Russell topped a rain-hit Las Vegas second practice for Mercedes ahead of Gasly and Leclerc; qualifying and the race follow this weekend. With Antonelli already the 2026 champion, the Vegas fight is for runner-up. Reported by Sky Sports.

items.headline: Update: Nicholls' 175 not out and Phillips' ton lift New Zealand to 368 against India
items.summary: At stumps on day two of the first Test in Wellington, Nicholls finished 175* and Phillips made 118 to take New Zealand to 368 (Bumrah four wickets); India reached 159 for one, Jaiswal 85, trailing by 209.

items.headline: Medvedev beats Tiafoe to claim the last ATP Finals semifinal spot in Turin
items.summary: Daniil Medvedev beat Frances Tiafoe in Turin to take the final ATP Finals semifinal place, setting up a meeting with world No. 1 Alexander Zverev; Alcaraz faces Shelton in the other semifinal. Reported by ATP Tour.

items.headline: Alcaraz downs Cobolli to top his group and reach the ATP Finals semifinals
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Flavio Cobolli in straight sets to top his group at the ATP Finals and reach the last four unbeaten in round-robin play. Reported by ATP Tour.

items.headline: NASA pauses science on its Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter after faults
items.summary: NASA said on Nov 19 it paused science on the Perseverance rover (main UHF radio failed Oct 30) and the 25-year-old Odyssey orbiter (a reaction wheel stopped); it hopes to resume by late November.

items.headline: Researchers unveil a first-of-its-kind blood test for the brain disease CTE
items.summary: Scientists reported a first-of-its-kind blood test for CTE, now diagnosable only after death; in a JAMA study of 21 former footballers who donated their brains, blood biomarkers flagged the most severe cases. Reported by Scientific American.

items.headline: A new obesity definition that goes beyond BMI outperforms the old one in a global study
items.summary: A study of 844,108 adults found a 2025 framework defining obesity by waist measures and organ function, not BMI alone, diagnosed obesity and predicted mortality better than BMI-based criteria. Published in Nature.

items.headline: Satellite data upends the idea of an evergreen Amazon, finding many trees go leafless
items.summary: High-resolution satellite data shows many Amazon trees stay leafless longer than expected, challenging the view of the rainforest as mostly evergreen and complicating carbon-cycle models. Published in Nature on Nov 18.

fun_fact.headline: In the 1830s, ketchup was sold as medicine
fun_fact.body: In the 1830s United States, ketchup was sold as medicine. The physician John Cook Bennett promoted concentrated tomato pills as a cure for indigestion and diarrhoea, and newspapers filled with advertisements for tomato extract. The fad collapsed around 1850, after some 'tomato pills' were found to contain no tomato at all.

puzzle.title: Room with No Chair
puzzle.body: A man is found dead, hanging from the ceiling of a completely empty, locked room. His feet dangle a metre above the floor. The only thing in the room with him is a puddle of water. There is no furniture and nothing he could have climbed on. How did he reach the noose?
puzzle.approach: Everything you need is in the description. The puddle is the clue: it points to something that was there but is no longer in its original form.
puzzle.answer: He stood on a large block of ice. After fixing the noose, he stepped off (or waited); the block slowly melted, leaving only the puddle of water and no stool, chair, or box for investigators to find.

word_puzzle.title: Common Ground
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four: ROYAL, CORPORAL, DECK, HOLLAND, TEAL, BOW, HANKS, GENERAL, PORT, AZURE, CRUISE, MAJOR, NAVY, HARDY, STERN, PRIVATE.
word_puzzle.approach: Several words look like they fit two groups; find the one split where every group is exactly four.
word_puzzle.answer: Shades of blue: NAVY, ROYAL, TEAL, AZURE. Military ranks: MAJOR, PRIVATE, GENERAL, CORPORAL. Famous Toms (actors): HANKS, CRUISE, HOLLAND, HARDY. Parts of a ship: DECK, PORT, BOW, STERN.

notes: Degraded-network run: the WebSearch crawler could not reach most allowed primary outlets (BBC, Reuters, AP, The Guardian, NYT, Sky News for search, CNA, The Straits Times, SCMP, The Verge, Ars Technica, Wired, FT, WSJ, all Indian primary outlets, Cricbuzz, New Scientist). Reachable allowed/fallback outlets were used (Mothership, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, CNBC, TechCrunch, Sky Sports, Formula1.com, ATP Tour, ESPNcricinfo index, NASA, Nature, Scientific American). India ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, CNBC) because every primary Indian outlet was unreachable after multiple retries, and yielded 3 verifiable items. UK News ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, CNN) because BBC and Sky News were unreachable; it reached only 2 verifiable UK-domestic items. Singapore reached 3 verifiable Mothership-sourced items. These three sections render fewer than the 4-item floor for reachability reasons, not lack of events, and were not padded. Total verified items across the brief: 28 (well above the 8-item hard-stop). ~60 searches and multiple retries made. F1: the Las Vegas race had not run at publish time, so a practice item was used, not a race result. Cricket: no deep-link ESPNcricinfo match URL was indexable, so the day-two scorecard (scores corroborated across multiple reports) links to the ESPNcricinfo WTC fixtures hub. No spectrum blocks were used because three distinct real-outlet framings could not be sourced under the network restrictions.
